source_text: My sense is that "Pooling over near-variant policies, or diverse retractions" is a premature question until we see some examples showing what cascades do (whether pooled or unpooled), what they look like, and what their specification is, so that cascadePolicySet is no longer a backdoor for "whatever" data structure we put in.  You could work with Codex to clarify the definitions and ideally prepare some real examples for me to look at in a blog post for zone.hyperreal.enterprises (Caddy)

reply_text:
A first draft of the post is up for you to look at: https://zone.hyperreal.enterprises/2026-09-30-what-a-cascade-is.html

It is not linked from the index and carries a noindex tag. The Lean section is a placeholder: I asked Codex-6 for the definitions in this turn and they have not come back.

**What is in it.**

- **Working definitions** in plain words, each with the countable thing it stands for: library, target, reading, unit, cascade, reading cascade, pattern graph, retraction, policy, and the policy set of a target. The policy set is defined as the output of a construction from the library, the reading, the pinned graph, k and the weights.
- **What a cascade does:** the round-by-round rule, with the chain-against-unordered example Codex-6 proved.
- **Seven real policy sets, 27 policies, each drawn.** Rows are the earliest round a unit can be attempted; roots are shaded. Each has its source text, the fragments 象 cited patterns for, and its F and G terms. Three are shown in full (M-web-arxana-ui-improvements, M-essays-diachronic-model, M-self-documenting-stack) and four are folded.
- **What the examples show that is wrong or unsettled,** as a numbered list.

**Things the examples make visible.**

- **Alphabetical arrows:** in the retraction drawings, edges whose direction came from the alphabet are dashed brown. For the M-self-documenting-stack retraction I checked, that is every edge.
- **A reading of boilerplate:** M-web-arxana-ui-improvements has an empty HEAD. Its reading is of the template sentence every mission file starts with, and its policy set still has six cascades. This was the best single policy in the joint run.
- **Near-copies:** the three M-self-documenting-stack retractions differ by one connector.

**What I checked.** The page serves (HTTP 200). I rendered two of the 27 drawings to images and looked at them; one needed its margins and labels fixed, which I did. The renderer I used does not draw arrowheads, so I have not seen them; a browser should. I have not viewed the page in a browser.

**Dispatched to Codex-6: the Lean definitions.** A reading, a cascade with proofs that its labels are library patterns and its ordering has no cycle, and a policy set that can only be obtained from the construction. The failing controls include a hand-written list being refused where a policy set is required. If the code does something the definitions cannot describe, they stop and report.

- Job: `invoke-1790781032893-29162-c59d4cca`
- Park: `park-41e534cd-7da6-4262-8c3b-42fb267643b1`, two-hour deadline

**Still running with Codex-4:**

- Sources for the 89 targets without a file: `park-bf6fc6f0-235a-4197-8ee0-4e886ba19176`
- The fix for alphabetical direction in retractions: `park-035d3a1b-974f-40ef-aad0-b574b87357cb`

I will regenerate the post when the direction fix and the Lean land. The generator and exporter are committed in futon2 (`6af24742b`), under `holes/labs/wm-contract/post-what-a-cascade-is/`.

The pooling question is set aside, as you said. Which C scores the cascades, the 192 mission readings and the restart are still with you, and none of them blocks the post.

No clicks were fired and nothing was loaded into the JVM.
